1 Executive Summary

This project replaces blanket discounting with a decision system. For every customer it answers: will they respond to a reward, which reward suits them, and who should we contact first.

Headline result. Five algorithms were benchmarked on identical pipelines with no pre-selected winner. The selected model (Logistic Regression) reached a test F1 of 0.7619 and a ROC-AUC of 0.8898. The reward engine then deployed 8 distinct reward types rather than a single blanket offer, and ML targeting returned 1.36x the net value of random targeting on an equal budget.

Why F1 and not accuracy

A false positive is a discount handed to someone who would have bought anyway — a margin leak. A false negative is a reachable customer left alone — a revenue leak. Neither error obviously dominates, so the balanced F1 score is the honest selection criterion. The winner was chosen dynamically from measured results, not assumed in advance.

7 The Reward Engine

This is the business core. It is not a threshold rule. For every customer the engine evaluates the entire reward catalogue and selects the offer with the best expected net value, under a campaign budget.

Two cost models, deliberately

  • Discount offers (percentage, rupee) reduce the price the customer pays. The cost appears as a smaller realised order value — it is already inside the margin.
  • Contingent offers (cashback, BOGO) are paid out after a successful purchase. They are a genuine extra outflow, incurred only by responders.
Conflating the two double-counts the discount — a classic promotion-P&L error. Keeping the accounting separate is what stops the engine from systematically over-spending.

10 Limitations

  1. The target is synthetic. reward_response was generated, not observed. Every model metric is a methodological result.
  2. The uplift model is a behavioural assumption. The response lift assigned to each offer is a parameter, not an estimate from an experiment.
  3. Expected values are illustrative, not financial forecasts.
  4. No causal inference. The model predicts association, not the causal effect of a reward. Randomised holdout testing is the only way to measure true lift.
  5. Moderate dataset size (1,401 customers). Confidence intervals on precision and recall are non-trivial at this scale.

The honest bottom line

This project delivers a complete, leak-free, reproducible decision pipeline: validated data, disciplined feature engineering, a fair five-model comparison, an explainable winner, and a cost-aware reward engine with a quantified simulation. It does not deliver a claim about real-world results, because the data to support such a claim does not exist here. Any project that skipped that distinction would be overselling.

Recommendations

RecommendationExpected effect
Replace blanket discounts with the ranked top-decile campaign Same budget, materially more responders
Use contingent offers for price-sensitive customers Response without a permanent price cut
Reserve deep percentage offers for lapsed high-value customers Reactivation where deep cuts are justified
Attach category coupons to each customer's top affinity Higher redemption on offers that fit
Run a randomised holdout campaign Converts every assumption in this report into a measurement

11 How This Report Was Produced

The entire pipeline ran automatically in 12 seconds:

  1. Synthetic dataset generated and validated (9,800 orders, 1,401 customers)
  2. 50 customer-level features built strictly inside the observation window (Jan–Sep 2025)
  3. Temporal leakage independently verified — features are reproducible without any campaign-window row
  4. Five models trained on identical pipelines; best selected dynamically on F1
  5. All customers scored; reward engine evaluated the full catalogue per customer
  6. Campaign prioritised, budget-matched simulation run, artefacts persisted

Everything is reproducible with RANDOM_STATE = 42. The full code, notebook and README are included in the project repository.
